newsitem.title: PERU: Flash flood kills five in Peru's southeast Andes.
newsitem.headline: Flash flood kills five in Peru's southeast Andes.

text.p: Five people were killed in a flash flood in Peru's southeastern Andes on Sunday and three rivers were flooded in torrential rains, authorities said.
The flash flood destroyed 12 homes and inundated 40 others in towns near Abancay, some 300 miles (480 km) from Lima, civil defence officials and local authorities said.
Among those killed were a 3-year-old girl, a 17-year-old boy and a mother and two other children whose ages were not available.
Civil Defence officials said the heavy rains caused flooding on the nearby San Antonio, Querapata and Condebamba Rivers near the Ampay National Sanctuary.

Park director Patricia Flores said the rains continued and were filling a reservoir that threatened to overflow and destroy the sanctuary. "If the rains continue, this ecological station will be swept away," she told Reuters by telephone.
The period between January and March is the rainy season in Peru's Andes when mudslides and flash floods, known locally as "huaycos," are common.
